text:
Moritz Seider is still the Red Wings' everything on the back end: 25:52 a night, 64 blocked shots, and a power-play role that has produced 8 of his 15 points. Evolving-Hockey ranked him third among 215 defensemen in wins above replacement last season, at both ends of the ice, which is the standard he's carrying into this one.

This season reads quieter. At five on five Detroit gets 47% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him out there, 3.1 points worse than when he sits, a real step back from last year's numbers. Some of that is the load: he played 30:12 in Tampa on November 3 and has topped 27 minutes four times in the last ten.

The goals are the other piece. One goal on 42 shots, a 2.4% shooting rate against a usual range near 5.5%. He has a 96 mph shot (92nd percentile) and isn't getting rewarded for it. With 60 points last season, his 15 in 24 games is below form. Our range still projects 46 to 67 points. We'd watch the five-on-five share more than the goals.
